Shri Kishore Shrivastava, learned Senior Advocate with Shri  Kunal Thakre, Advocate for the petitioner.
 Shri Rahul Sethi, learned GA for the respondent/State.

Heard on I.A.No.460/2018.
sh

The respondents have filed an application for vacating the e stay mainly on the ground that the petitioner is having remedy of ad appeal under Section 46(4) of the Food Safety & Standards Act,
2006, Pr hence, stay be vacated and petition be dismissed.

Shri Bagadiya has produced copy of the order dated 01.02.2016 a hy passed by the coordinate bench of this Court in W.P.No.2665/2013, by which the similar application for vacating of stay on the ground that of ad availability of alternate efficacious remedy has been rejected.
The M relevant para of the order dated 01.02.2016, passed by the Gwalior Bench of this Court is reproduced below:
of "I.A.No.309/16, an application for dismissal of the petition filed by the rt State primarily raises three grounds.

The first being that the petitioner can ou approach the Food Safely Appellate Tribunal under Section 70 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (in short the Act, 2006) against the order of C Adjudicating Officer under Section 68 of the Act.

Further, it is contended that h vide Annexure-A/2 (alongwith I.A.No.309/16), the coordinate bench at ig principal seat in W.P.No.19958/13 has relegated the petitioner therein to avail H the remedy of appeal and lastly by relying on Annexure-A/3, it is contended that similar petitions have been dismissed by the single bench at the principal seat.
The present petition assails the prosecution launched against the petitioner and also sanction granted for prosecuting the petitioner under the said Act, 2006 on various grounds.
In the instant case, the petitioner's product, i.e. cream biscuits have been found to be misbranded.

Thus,
final adjudication by the adjudicating authority has not yet taken place and therefore the question of availing alternative efficacious remedy does not arise."
Even otherwise, this petition is pending since 2014 and interim order is still in operation.
Thereafter, the petition has been admitted and the respondent has been permitted to make a mention for out of turn hearing.

Learned senior counsel for the petitioner fairly submits that petitioners are interested in early disposal of this petition as number of petitions are pending before all the Itc Limited vs State Of M.P. And Anr. on 14 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156774845/
1 three benches of this Court.

sentences.text: When the petitioners are ready for argument of their petitions finally, the question of vacating of interim relief does not arises for limited period.
The respondents are having liberty to approach the Division Bench for request of out of turn hearing of these writ petitions.

I.A.No.460/2018 is accordingly rejected.
